findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the FULL plan_review_status verdict vocabulary in B2 and classify EVERY value into accept/flag/fail-open, explicitly deciding that transient-failure verdicts (unavailable/error) fail OPEN (no BLOCK) so they cannot cause the mechanical FPs AC line 4 forbids.
evidence: Plan B2 partitions the verdict enum into ACCEPTED {certified, stale-code, stale-head} and FLAG {unsigned, stale-material, stale-reopened} — 6 values total.

attest_gate.py:167-168 plan_review_status docstring: verdict is 'certified … else one of stale-code / stale-head / stale-material / stale-reopened / unsigned / wrong-kind / malformed-pin / unverifiable-material / error'.

compute_validity (attest.py) also emits verdicts the plan never names: 'unverifiable-material' (line 729, when the material fingerprint can't be recomputed — fail-closed), 'incompatible-phase' (742), 'malformed-pin' (629), 'malformed-phase' (636), and dynamic pin-status verdicts (749).

docs/plan-review-gate.md:891-894 confirms the full set includes 'unverifiable-material, stale-pin-drift, stale-pin-missing, malformed-pin, incompatible-phase, malformed-phase, and unavailable' and that 'An unexpected local read, parser, or signature failure is fail-closed as unavailable'.

The plan's B2 default-BLOCK bucket therefore blocks on 'unavailable'/'error' — a transient read/verify failure, not an absent attestation — which is a mechanical false positive contradicting AC line 4 ('zero mechanical FPs').
findings.finding: The B2 DET criterion keys on the plan_review_status verdict enum but the plan enumerates only 6 of its ≥13 possible values; the rule 'verdict NOT IN {certified,stale-code,stale-head} -> BLOCK' silently buckets every unenumerated verdict into BLOCK, including the fail-closed transient-failure verdict, which produces mechanical false positives the plan's own AC forbids.
findings.location: Approach B2 / Acceptance Criteria line 3 ('Verdict predicate accepts certified/stale-code/stale-head, flags unsigned/stale-material/stale-reopened')
scenarios: A review-bot checkout hits a transient signature/parser/read failure on an oversized bug fix → verdict 'unavailable'/'error' → NOT IN accepted set → BLOCKS a fix whose author did review the plan (mechanical FP).

An oversized bug fix whose attestation is 'unverifiable-material' or 'incompatible-phase' → falls into BLOCK by omission, but the plan never states whether these should block or how the teaching message should differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Define three explicit buckets keyed on the real enum (attest_gate.py:167-168 + docs/plan-review-gate.md:891-894): ACCEPTED = {certified, stale-code, stale-head}; FLAG/BLOCK = {unsigned, stale-material, stale-reopened} and the deterministic staleness verdicts {unverifiable-material, malformed-pin, malformed-phase, incompatible-phase, stale-pin-drift, stale-pin-missing, wrong-kind}; FAIL-OPEN (no finding) = {unavailable, error} transient read/verify failures. Add unit cases for unavailable->no-finding and unverifiable-material->BLOCK to the B2 matrix.
